0.long_answer: Punctate inner choroidopathy (PIC) is a form of inflammatory choroiditis that is commonly classified among the White Dot Syndromes. It primarily affects young myopic women and is distinguished by the absence of significant inflammation in the anterior chamber and vitreous humor. Unlike other inflammatory diseases of the eye that involve extensive intraocular inflammation, PIC typically presents with small, punctate lesions at the level of the choroid without the usual inflammatory markers in the front portions of the eye. This clinical profile helps differentiate PIC from other similar chorioretinopathies and is a key factor in its diagnosis and management.
